samples.summary: `weights` is interpolated into the Google Fonts css2 URL without encoding, and it now flows from a DOM `data-` attribute
samples.evidence: `familyParam()` builds `family=${encodeURIComponent(family)}:wght@${weights ?? DEFAULT_WEIGHTS}` — the family is encoded, the weight string is not. This change adds a new path into it: both observers read `row.dataset.fontWeights` (font-family-picker.tsx:152, more-fonts-dialog.tsx:154) and pass it to `ensurePreviewFontLink`, which forwards it through `previewWeight()` (only `.split(';')[0].trim()`, no validation) into the same unencoded slot. A weights value containing `&` would inject additional query parameters into the css2 request (e.g. `400&text=…&family=…`). Today every source of that attribute is static bundled catalog data (`font-catalog.data.ts` / `font-catalog.full.ts`), so I could not build an end-to-end exploit, and the scheme/host/path prefix in `css2Url` is a constant, so the request cannot be redirected off `fonts.googleapis.com`. Impact is therefore bounded to altering the parameters of a third-party font request. Hardening: run the weight through `encodeURIComponent` or validate it against `/^[0-9;.,]+$/` at the boundary now that untrusted-looking DOM state feeds it.

samples.summary: `hasFullFamilyLink` identifies the Google Fonts origin with a substring test on the whole href instead of an origin check
samples.evidence: `if (!href.includes('fonts.googleapis.com')) continue;` treats any stylesheet link whose URL merely *contains* that string as a Google Fonts link — e.g. `https://attacker.example/x.css?ref=fonts.googleapis.com&family=Inter` satisfies both this test and the `family=` scan on line 274, so `hasFullFamilyLink('Inter')` returns true and the preview injection is suppressed. The same loose match means an `https://fonts.googleapis.com.evil.test/...` link is trusted as the real origin. The security consequence here is limited (the only decision it gates is whether to add a preview `<link>`, so the worst outcome is a font rendering in a fallback face), but parsing the href with `new URL(href).hostname === 'fonts.googleapis.com'` is the correct check and costs nothing.

samples.summary: New third-party egress channel: arbitrary caller-supplied text is placed in a URL sent to fonts.googleapis.com, with no restriction on what may be passed
samples.evidence: `ensurePreviewFontLink(family, text)` puts `encodeURIComponent(uniqueChars(text))` into the `&text=` query of a request to `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...` (line 326-329). The two current callers pass `row.textContent` of picker rows, which is only a font family name plus a group label — I traced both (font-family-picker.tsx:149, more-fonts-dialog.tsx:151) and neither carries document or user-typed content, so nothing sensitive leaks today. The residual risk is that the function's contract ("pass whatever the element paints") invites a future caller to hand it rendered *document* text, which would then be transmitted verbatim in a URL to a third party (and land in that party's logs, plus local browser history). Worth a one-line contract note that `text` must never be user content, or a caller-side allowlist. There is no app-wide CSP in the repo (only `frame-ancestors` on one backend route, packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:166) constraining this egress.
